text:
sara: Quick sync — I pushed a small prototype for a consolidated access gateway that runs pre-fanout auth checks and emits a compact allow/deny token for downstream query workers. Thoughts?

mike: saw it, skimmed. what's the perf hit on p99?

sara: measured on my laptop (dev profile) — additional ~4ms median, p99 ~12ms extra when cache miss. with local LRU for token re-use it's closer to 2ms median. numbers in the PR.

jamal: that p99 seems fine BUT curious about cache cold-start with large tenant counts. do we plan per-tenant namespaces or a shared cache with tagging?

sara: prototype uses shared cache keyed by (tenant, route). We discussed shards in the doc; downside is memory & complexity. advantage is simpler rollback.

nina: long-term I'd prefer per-tenant admission so noisy neighbor can be limited. but that implies per-tenant caches + rehydration logic. ops will need instrumentation to monitor OOM/excess evictions.

mike: also: how do we map RBAC policy changes? if a policy update is applied, how do downstream query workers see that quickly without ripping caches?

sara: two options: 1) short TTLs (100ms-1s) + publish invalidation events; 2) stash policy version in token and let workers validate version mismatch and re-check from gateway.

jamal: option 2 seems safer for correctness. workers can fallback to consulting gateway on version mismatch. implementation sketch: token = {allow:true, policy_v: 42, sig:...} and worker checks policy_v against its local policy_v; if mismatch, call gateway.

mike: that adds a roundtrip on mismatch — acceptable if mismatches are rare. need to ensure gateway is horizontally autoscalable and cheap.

nina: how about routing for large dashboards that fan out to many shards? gateway should be able to answer bulk permission queries (batch API) to avoid N x 1.

sara: agreed — I added a batch endpoint in the PR: POST /v1/auth/batch with payload of routes. returns map of route->token. uses internal batching + KV prefix scan to reduce DB hits.

mike: any security concerns with tokens being passed between services? plaintext vs signed? expiry?

sara: tokens are signed (HMAC) and include expiry (default 10s). workers verify signature. also support introspect endpoint for debug.

jamal: what about ephemeral credentials across private deployments (on-prem)? HSM/KMS integration needed for signing key rotation. ops-bot should create rotation plan.

ops-bot: deploy: canary succeeded for commit sha a1b2c3; gateway pod CPU ~10% on canary under synthetic load.

nina: nice. next steps: 1) add eviction metrics and per-tenant tag counters, 2) add policy-version propagation test in e2e harness, 3) run tenancy loadbench to validate memory growth.

mike: also add circuit-breaker: if gateway latency spikes, workers should have fallback policy (deny-by-default or optimistic-allow with audit). which default do we want?

jamal: deny-by-default is safer. but for non-sensitive dashboards maybe optimistic-allow. need per-route policy on fallback behavior.

sara: I'll update PR with config snippet for route-level behavior. current draft: ```json
{
  "routes": {
    "dashboards.read": {"fallback": "deny", "cache_ttl_ms": 500},
    "health.check": {"fallback": "allow", "cache_ttl_ms": 2000}
  }
}
```

mike: looks good. let's also add a note in the console SLO doc about acceptable p99 delta when gateway is enabled and a plan to experiment with offloading simple allow predicates to client-side evaluation to shave microseconds.

sara: will do. thanks all — I'll iterate on the PR and schedule a short arch review tomorrow. :thumbsup:
